sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是《99%隐形》。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: In a lot of ways, Lincoln Heights, Ohio, sounds just like any other suburb.
sentences.zh: 在很多方面，俄亥俄州的林肯高地听起来和其他郊区没什么两样。

sentences.en: If you walk around town, you'll hear kids playing outside the local elementary school.
sentences.zh: 如果你在镇上走走，会听到孩子们在当地小学外玩耍的声音。

sentences.en: You'll hear the highway that takes commuters down to Cincinnati.
sentences.zh: 你会听到通勤者前往辛辛那提的高速公路传来的车流声。

sentences.en: At the woods on the edge of town, the bird song is delightful.
sentences.zh: 在镇边缘的树林里，鸟鸣声悦耳动听。

sentences.en: Lincoln Heights is small, less than one square mile with about 3,100 people.
sentences.zh: 林肯高地很小，面积不到一平方英里，人口约3100人。

sentences.en: Christina Cotarucci is a senior writer at Slate.
sentences.zh: 克里斯蒂娜·科塔鲁奇是《Slate》杂志的资深撰稿人。

sentences.en: It's a quiet, residential place that seems far from the bustle of the city,
sentences.zh: 这是一个安静的居住区，似乎远离城市的喧嚣，

sentences.en: even though it's just 13 miles north of Cincinnati.
sentences.zh: 尽管它距离辛辛那提以北仅13英里。

sentences.en: It's the kind of place where everyone knows everyone.
sentences.zh: 这是一个每个人都认识每个人的地方。

sentences.en: If you live there, it's hard to get anywhere in town without someone stopping you to say hi.
sentences.zh: 如果你住在那儿，很难在镇上走动而不被熟人拦下打招呼。

sentences.en: There are well-kept single-family homes and low-lying apartment complexes.
sentences.zh: 那里有维护良好的独栋住宅和低矮的公寓大楼。

sentences.en: People gather in their grassy backyards for cookouts and in parking lots for pickup basketball games.
sentences.zh: 人们聚集在草木葱茏的后院举行烧烤，在停车场进行街头篮球比赛。

sentences.en: The town feels calm and peaceful, at least until the gunfire starts.
sentences.zh: 小镇感觉宁静祥和，至少在枪声响起之前是这样。

sentences.en: Most weekdays, it begins in the morning and lasts through the afternoon.
sentences.zh: 大多数工作日，枪声从早晨开始，一直持续到下午。

sentences.en: Sometimes it goes past sundown and occasionally into the weekends.
sentences.zh: 有时会持续到日落之后，偶尔还会延续到周末。

sentences.en: Once the shooting begins, it comes in rapid-fire waves throughout the day.
sentences.zh: 一旦射击开始，全天都会传来密集的枪声。

sentences.en: People say it makes it hard to focus or relax.
sentences.zh: 人们说这让他们难以集中注意力或放松休息。

sentences.en: And those who work the night shift say they can't sleep.
sentences.zh: 而那些上夜班的人说他们根本无法入睡。

sentences.en: Residents worry about what the gunfire is doing to their hearing and their stress levels.
sentences.zh: 居民们担心枪声对他们的听力和压力水平造成的影响。

sentences.en: They're especially concerned about their kids, who are listening to gunshots all day long while they're trying to play or study.
sentences.zh: 他们尤其担心自己的孩子，孩子们在玩耍或学习时整天都要听着枪声。

sentences.en: The noise of gunfire isn't from street violence.
sentences.zh: 这些枪声并非来自街头暴力。

sentences.en: It all comes from an open-air gun range that's owned by the Cincinnati Police Department.
sentences.zh: 它们全部来自辛辛那提警察局拥有的一个露天靶场。

sentences.en: This thing is huge, the size of about 22 football fields.
sentences.zh: 这个靶场非常巨大，大约有22个足球场那么大。

sentences.en: It sits just outside of Lincoln Heights, right along the town's northern border.
sentences.zh: 它就坐落在林肯高地外，紧邻小镇的北部边界。

sentences.en: And the cops use it a lot.
sentences.zh: 而且警察经常使用它。

sentences.en: In 2019, the department reported that officers train there about 300 days out of the year.
sentences.zh: 2019年，该部门报告称，警员每年有大约300天在那里进行训练。

sentences.en: The constant, nerve-frying sound from that gun range has been plaguing Lincoln Heights for the last 75 years.
sentences.zh: 过去75年来，靶场传出的持续且令人神经紧绷的噪音一直困扰着林肯高地。

sentences.en: That noise truly was just like bird chirping.
sentences.zh: 那噪音听起来真的就像鸟叫一样。

sentences.en: It was just like your environment.
sentences.zh: 就像你周围的环境音一样。

sentences.en: You just grew up with it.
sentences.zh: 你只是在那种环境中长大的。

sentences.en: That's Durrance Daniels.
sentences.zh: 那是杜兰斯·丹尼尔斯。

sentences.en: He's a town council member in Lincoln Heights.
sentences.zh: 他是林肯高地的镇议会议员。

sentences.en: His family goes back five generations to when the town was founded.
sentences.zh: 他的家族在这里生活了五代，可以追溯到小镇建立之初。

sentences.en: He went away to college in North Carolina.
sentences.zh: 他曾去北卡罗来纳州上大学。

sentences.en: And one Thanksgiving break, he brought his roommate home to visit.
sentences.zh: 有一次感恩节假期，他带室友回家做客。

sentences.en: We were just kind of outside, just kind of hanging out.
sentences.zh: 我们当时就在外面，随便闲逛。

sentences.en: And he could just constantly hear that boom, boom, boom, boom sound.
sentences.zh: 他能一直听到那种砰、砰、砰、砰的声音。

sentences.en: And we're right in front of my parents' house.
sentences.zh: 当时我们就在我父母家门前。

sentences.en: He just literally just looks at me and says,
sentences.zh: 他直勾勾地看着我问：

sentences.en: D, what is that noise?
sentences.zh: “D，那是什么声音？”

sentences.en: Like, who's over there shooting?
sentences.zh: “是谁在那边开枪？”

sentences.en: Like, what's all that going on?
sentences.zh: “到底发生了什么？”

sentences.en: You know, it's just the gun range.
sentences.zh: “你知道，那只是靶场。”

sentences.en: Like, you know, you know, it's just kind of what we...
sentences.zh: “你知道，你知道，这只是我们……”

sentences.en: Like, y'all just live around that every day?
sentences.zh: “你们每天就生活在那种环境下？”

sentences.en: Like, that's just kind of what y'all just deal with every day?
sentences.zh: “你们每天都要忍受这些？”

sentences.en: It was the first time Durrance had really thought about it.
sentences.zh: 这是杜兰斯第一次真正思考这个问题。

sentences.en: About how he wasn't even startled by something that was alarming to anyone who didn't live there.
sentences.zh: 思考为什么他甚至不会对这种让外人感到惊恐的声音感到惊讶。

sentences.en: That kind of just, you know, it was awakening for me that this isn't normal.
sentences.zh: 那对我来说是一种觉醒，让我意识到这并不正常。

sentences.en: As if living with the relentless sound of gunfire wasn't bad enough,
sentences.zh: 仿佛生活在持续不断的枪声中还不够糟糕，

sentences.en: there are a lot of things that make the situation even worse.
sentences.zh: 还有很多事情让情况变得更糟。

sentences.en: This is nonstop police gunfire bombarding a town where almost all of the residents are black.
sentences.zh: 这是警察在几乎全是黑人居民的小镇上进行不间断的实弹射击。

sentences.en: And Cincinnati police, the cops who practice there,
sentences.zh: 而辛辛那提警察，那些在那里训练的警察，

sentences.en: don't even patrol Lincoln Heights or any of the other towns around the range.
sentences.zh: 甚至不在林肯高地或靶场周围的任何城镇巡逻。

sentences.en: So these are out-of-towners coming to let off shots in Lincoln Heights' backyard.
sentences.zh: 所以这些外来者来到林肯高地的后院开枪。

sentences.en: A majority of Lincoln Heights residents live below the poverty line.
sentences.zh: 大多数林肯高地的居民生活在贫困线以下。

sentences.en: And they can't help thinking that if their town were wealthier or whiter,
sentences.zh: 他们不禁想到，如果他们的城镇更富有或白人更多，

sentences.en: the city of Cincinnati would never get away with this.
sentences.zh: 辛辛那提市绝不敢这么做。

sentences.en: When I started reporting on this gun range,
sentences.zh: 当我开始报道这个靶场时，

sentences.en: I was expecting to get a straightforward story about a particularly disturbing kind of noise pollution.
sentences.zh: 我本以为会写出一个关于某种特别令人不安的噪音污染的直白故事。

sentences.en: But there's another layer to it.
sentences.zh: 但这件事还有另一层含义。

sentences.en: Because Lincoln Heights isn't just any suburb.
sentences.zh: 因为林肯高地不仅仅是一个普通的郊区。

sentences.en: It's the first black self-governed town north of the Mason-Dixon line,
sentences.zh: 它是梅森-迪克森线以北第一个由黑人自治的城镇，

sentences.en: founded almost a century ago with ambitions of becoming a sprawling, self-sufficient community.
sentences.zh: 近一个世纪前建立时，怀揣着成为一个广阔、自给自足社区的雄心。

sentences.en: That vision never fully came to pass.
sentences.zh: 那个愿景从未完全实现。

sentences.en: And today, the bullets that echo through town are a daily reminder
sentences.zh: 而今天，在镇上回荡的枪声每天都在提醒人们，

sentences.en: of how the founders' dreams for Lincoln Heights were obstructed right from the start.
sentences.zh: 林肯高地创始人的梦想从一开始就受到了阻碍。

sentences.en: During the Great Migration,
sentences.zh: 在大迁徙期间，

sentences.en: Durrance Daniels' great-grandfather and his great-great-grandfather
sentences.zh: 杜兰斯·丹尼尔斯的曾祖父和高祖父

sentences.en: joined a group of others making their way from rural Georgia up to southern Ohio.
sentences.zh: 加入了从佐治亚州农村前往俄亥俄州南部的迁徙大军。

sentences.en: A lot of the men first started moving up towards this area in the early 1920s,
sentences.zh: 很多男性在20世纪20年代初开始向这个地区迁移，

sentences.en: late, you know, 19-teens.
sentences.zh: 也就是1910年代末。

sentences.en: My grandmother, my great-grandmother, and my great-great-grandmother,
sentences.zh: 我的祖母、曾祖母和高祖母，

sentences.en: they also kind of came up with my aunts a year after that.
sentences.zh: 她们也在那之后一年带着我的姑姑们搬了过来。

sentences.en: The folks that were leaving the South, this first wave of migrants,
sentences.zh: 那些离开南方的人，也就是第一批移民，

sentences.en: were individuals who were filled with hope and the possibilities of a better life.
sentences.zh: 是充满希望和对美好生活憧憬的个体。

sentences.en: Henry Louis Taylor Jr.
sentences.zh: 亨利·路易斯·泰勒二世

sentences.en: is a professor at the University at Buffalo
sentences.zh: 是布法罗大学的教授，

sentences.en: and an expert on the history of Lincoln Heights.
sentences.zh: 也是林肯高地历史方面的专家。

sentences.en: They were very high-spirited individuals who believed in hard work
sentences.zh: 他们是非常有活力的人，相信勤劳工作，

sentences.en: and wanted to be in a situation to control their own lives and their own destinies.
sentences.zh: 并希望能够掌控自己的生活和命运。

sentences.en: As one of the Lincoln Heights residents said to me,
sentences.zh: 正如一位林肯高地居民对我所说：

sentences.en: I came here to live better and to do better.
sentences.zh: “我来这里是为了生活得更好，做得更好。”

sentences.en: After crossing the Ohio River, which separates northern Kentucky from Cincinnati,
sentences.zh: 在跨越了将肯塔基州北部与辛辛那提隔开的俄亥俄河后，

sentences.en: the migrants first tried settling in the city.
sentences.zh: 移民们最初试图在城里定居。

sentences.en: But property was really expensive and racist real estate practices were rampant.
sentences.zh: 但那里的房产非常昂贵，种族主义房地产行为也很猖獗。

sentences.en: So they found a space 13 miles from Cincinnati where they were able to buy some land,
sentences.zh: 于是他们在距离辛辛那提13英里处找到了一块地方，在那里买了一些土地，

sentences.en: organize, and say, hey, let's create our own community.
sentences.zh: 组织起来，说：嘿，让我们建立自己的社区。

sentences.en: The spot they settled on was north of the city, deep in unincorporated Hamilton County.
sentences.zh: 他们选定的地点在城市以北，位于汉密尔顿县未建制的深处。

sentences.en: There was a lot of land there.
sentences.zh: 那里有很多土地。

sentences.en: And since it had no electrical grid and minimal running water, the acreage was cheap.
sentences.zh: 由于没有电网，自来水也很少，所以土地很便宜。

sentences.en: With plans to build a whole new town from scratch, the residents started homesteading in the 1920s.
sentences.zh: 怀揣着从零开始建设一个全新城镇的计划，居民们在20世纪20年代开始了定居生活。

sentences.en: These were people from rural areas.
sentences.zh: 这些人来自农村地区。

sentences.en: They weren't from the city.
sentences.zh: 他们不是城里人。

sentences.en: And so they knew how to build cisterns.
sentences.zh: 所以他们知道如何建造蓄水池。

sentences.en: They knew how to tap into the waters and build wells.
sentences.zh: 他们知道如何引水和打井。

sentences.en: So looking back at what they managed to accomplish with limited resources was quite astounding.
sentences.zh: 所以回顾他们以有限的资源所取得的成就，确实令人震惊。

sentences.en: Once a critical mass of Black people had settled in the area, those homesteaders had a realization.
sentences.zh: 当大量黑人在该地区定居后，这些定居者意识到了一件事。

sentences.en: In order to have any real power over their own lives, they needed more than just land.
sentences.zh: 为了对自己的人生拥有真正的掌控权，他们需要的不仅仅是土地。

sentences.en: They needed to govern their own space.
sentences.zh: 他们需要治理自己的空间。

sentences.en: And they knew, from living under Jim Crow, what it was like to be denied that autonomy.
sentences.zh: 而且他们从在吉姆·克劳法下的生活经历中，深知被剥夺这种自主权是什么滋味。

sentences.en: By the late 1930s, plans were underway to open an aircraft manufacturing plant in Hamilton County.
sentences.zh: 到20世纪30年代末，在汉密尔顿县开设一家飞机制造厂的计划正在进行中。

sentences.en: Once a rural no-man's land, that region would soon become an industrial hub.
sentences.zh: 那个曾经的农村无人区，很快就会成为一个工业中心。

sentences.en: So it was a lot of opportunity where an all-Black neighborhood was going to become an economic powerhouse right in the middle of Hamilton County.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个巨大的机会，一个全黑人社区将成为汉密尔顿县中心的一个经济强区。

sentences.en: It was already set for it.
sentences.zh: 一切都已经准备就绪。

sentences.en: So a group of residents took a county map and drew a set of ambitious boundaries around nearly 10 square miles in Hamilton County.
sentences.zh: 于是，一群居民拿着县地图，在汉密尔顿县近10平方英里的范围内划定了一系列雄心勃勃的边界。

sentences.en: The space encompassed the homes they'd built and lots of land primed for industrial development, plus plenty of room to grow.
sentences.zh: 这片空间不仅包含了他们建造的家园，还有大量适合工业开发的土地，以及充足的发展空间。

sentences.en: The map was part of a plan to incorporate all of that space into a single town.
sentences.zh: 这张地图是将所有这些空间合并为一个城镇计划的一部分。

sentences.en: It would be their town, a place they would control.
sentences.zh: 那将是他们的城镇，一个由他们掌控的地方。

sentences.en: They named it Lincoln Heights.
sentences.zh: 他们将其命名为林肯高地。

sentences.en: It was a brilliant strategy.
sentences.zh: 这是一个绝妙的策略。

sentences.en: They would have an industrial and an economic base to help support the community.
sentences.zh: 他们将拥有工业和经济基础来支持社区发展。

sentences.en: And that taxation would have allowed them to develop their schools, their roads, and would have created a level of prosperity that would not have existed before.
sentences.zh: 而这些税收本可以让他们发展学校、道路，并创造出前所未有的繁荣水平。

sentences.en: It was a bold move for an all-Black community to lay claim to this much land, especially with white towns nearby.
sentences.zh: 对于一个全黑人社区来说，宣称拥有这么多土地是一个大胆的举动，尤其是在附近还有白人城镇的情况下。

sentences.en: Henry says the founders were excited and full of hope.
sentences.zh: 亨利说，创始人们当时非常兴奋，充满希望。

sentences.en: In 1939, they presented their Lincoln Heights plan to the county for final approval.
sentences.zh: 1939年，他们将林肯高地计划提交给县政府进行最终审批。

sentences.en: But the white county leadership and the neighboring suburbs all put up immediate heavy resistance.
sentences.zh: 但白人县领导层和邻近的郊区都立即进行了强烈的抵制。

sentences.en: They were terrified that an expansive Black community would attract people from the so-called slums of Cincinnati out into the suburbs.
sentences.zh: 他们非常害怕一个扩张的黑人社区会把所谓的辛辛那提贫民窟的人吸引到郊区来。

sentences.en: And the idea of a small group of Black people getting a foothold was something nobody wanted to see happen.
sentences.zh: 而且一小群黑人获得立足点的想法是没人愿意看到的。

sentences.en: And there was a movement underway that simply attempted to wipe the town out.
sentences.zh: 当时甚至有一场运动试图直接抹掉这个城镇。

sentences.en: Hamilton County officials deliberately slow-walked the Lincoln Heights plan for seven years.
sentences.zh: 汉密尔顿县官员故意拖延了林肯高地计划长达七年之久。

sentences.en: In that time, a lot of other property in the proposal was snapped up by the surrounding towns.
sentences.zh: 在那段时间里，提案中的许多其他土地被周边城镇抢购一空。

sentences.en: Once whites begin to understand their ambition, they waged a relentless campaign designed to keep Blacks from acquiring these industrial lands.
sentences.zh: 一旦白人开始了解他们的雄心，他们就发动了一场无情的运动，旨在阻止黑人获得这些工业用地。

sentences.en: One critical piece of that land was an open-air gun range.
sentences.zh: 那片土地中关键的一块就是露天靶场。

sentences.en: It was 30 or so acres owned by a group of war veterans who had a shooting club.
sentences.zh: 那是大约30英亩的土地，由一群拥有射击俱乐部的退伍军人所有。

sentences.en: In 1946, the city of Cincinnati bought it as a place for its police to train.
sentences.zh: 1946年，辛辛那提市买下了它，作为警察的训练场所。

sentences.en: At that time, the only other building in the immediate area was a school for the deaf.
sentences.zh: 当时，附近唯一的其他建筑是一所聋哑学校。

sentences.en: The local Black community had asked for that parcel of land for themselves seven years earlier to develop Lincoln Heights.
sentences.zh: 当地黑人社区早在七年前就曾要求将那块地留给他们自己，以发展林肯高地。

sentences.en: If they had succeeded, you would probably be here telling a very, very different story.
sentences.zh: 如果他们成功了，你现在可能就在这里讲述一个非常、非常不同的故事。

sentences.en: Because they would have also had control over the land where the gun range was located.
sentences.zh: 因为他们也会拥有靶场所在土地的控制权。

sentences.en: And certainly they wouldn't have agreed to allow it to be placed there.
sentences.zh: 当然，他们绝不会同意让靶场设在那里。

sentences.en: In 1946, the same year the Cincinnati Police Department took ownership of the firing range,
sentences.zh: 1946年，也就是辛辛那提警察局接管靶场的同一年，

sentences.en: Lincoln Heights was finally approved for incorporation.
sentences.zh: 林肯高地终于获准成立。

sentences.en: But the Black residents only got a tenth of the land they'd originally set out to govern.
sentences.zh: 但黑人居民只得到了他们最初计划治理土地的十分之一。

sentences.en: Less than one square mile, shaped like a teacup.
sentences.zh: 不到一平方英里，形状像个茶杯。

sentences.en: Really, just the original housing settlement.
sentences.zh: 实际上，只是最初的住宅区。

sentences.en: With no aircraft manufacturer or any other big businesses.
sentences.zh: 没有飞机制造商，也没有任何其他大企业。

sentences.en: Yes, it was a victory.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是一场胜利。

sentences.en: They had created the first Black self-governing town north of the Mason-Dixon line.
sentences.zh: 他们创建了梅森-迪克森线以北第一个黑人自治城镇。

sentences.en: But they didn't have the industrial tax base or the open, developable land the town would have needed to thrive.
sentences.zh: 但他们没有城镇繁荣所需的工业税基或可开发的空地。

sentences.en: And to add insult to injury, because the way the county had divvied up the land, the Cincinnati Police Gun Range was now right on the border of Lincoln Heights.
sentences.zh: 更糟糕的是，由于县政府划分土地的方式，辛辛那提警察靶场现在正好位于林肯高地的边界上。

sentences.en: And because Lincoln Heights was granted precious little space for expansion, residents would ultimately end up living right next door.
sentences.zh: 而且由于林肯高地获准扩张的空间极小，居民们最终只能住在靶场隔壁。

sentences.en: But whatever nuisance the range presented, it wasn't enough to dull the shine of an all-Black town on the rise.
sentences.zh: 但无论靶场带来什么困扰，都无法掩盖一个正在崛起的全黑人城镇的光芒。

sentences.en: In the 1950s and 60s, the population of Lincoln Heights ballooned, small businesses thrived,
sentences.zh: 在20世纪50和60年代，林肯高地的人口激增，小企业蓬勃发展，

sentences.en: and the community started its own police force in town council.
sentences.zh: 社区还成立了自己的警察部队和镇议会。

sentences.en: The aircraft manufacturer became a general electric plant.
sentences.zh: 那家飞机制造商变成了通用电气工厂。

sentences.en: And although it wasn't in Lincoln Heights like the founders wanted, residents still got good jobs at GE.
sentences.zh: 虽然它不像创始人们希望的那样位于林肯高地，但居民们仍然在通用电气获得了不错的工作。

sentences.en: This is Wakanda, you ask my grandpa.
sentences.zh: 这就是瓦坎达，你去问我爷爷就知道了。

sentences.en: She said, we did it all.
sentences.zh: 她说，我们什么都做过。

sentences.en: I've literally heard, you name it, we did it.
sentences.zh: 我真的听过这种话，你说得出的，我们都做过。

sentences.en: We had everything here.
sentences.zh: 我们这里什么都有。

sentences.en: Durrance Daniels loves regaling his kids with stories from the town's glory days that he heard from his elders.
sentences.zh: 杜兰斯·丹尼尔斯喜欢给孩子们讲他从长辈那里听来的小镇辉煌时期的故事。

sentences.en: They would tell him, I'd work a job here, go to the grocery store here.
sentences.zh: 他们会告诉他，我在这里工作，在这里买菜。

sentences.en: I went to the pharmacy here.
sentences.zh: 我在这里的药店买药。

sentences.en: My dentist was here.
sentences.zh: 我的牙医就在这儿。

sentences.en: I went to go party here.
sentences.zh: 我在这里聚会。

sentences.en: Like, you know, everything was here, and you never had to leave it.
sentences.zh: 就像，你知道的，一切都在这里，你根本不需要离开。

sentences.en: Everybody looked like you, and everybody knew you, and everybody was essentially family in some aspect of it.
sentences.zh: 每个人看起来都和你一样，每个人都认识你，从某种程度上说，大家基本上就是一家人。

sentences.en: That sounds like paradise.
sentences.zh: 听起来像是天堂。

sentences.en: But of course, it wasn't perfect.
sentences.zh: 但当然，它并不完美。

sentences.en: Durrance's grandfather, Elbert Daniels, has lived in Lincoln Heights since before it was even called Lincoln Heights.
sentences.zh: 杜兰斯的祖父埃尔伯特·丹尼尔斯在林肯高地还没叫这个名字之前就住在这里了。

sentences.en: Oh yeah, I was born here in 1927.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的，我1927年就出生在这里。

sentences.en: Born down there on Beale Street.
sentences.zh: 出生在下面的比尔街。

sentences.en: In the 1970s, Elbert got elected to the town council, and he always told Durrance that when he thought back on his tenure, he had one big regret.
sentences.zh: 20世纪70年代，埃尔伯特当选为镇议员，他总是告诉杜兰斯，回想起自己的任期，他有一个巨大的遗憾。

sentences.en: Oh, the gun range, oh, years ago, when I got elected to the council, I couldn't get nobody on council to go along with me to start fighting it.
sentences.zh: 哦，那个射击场，多年前我刚当选议员时，我没法让议会里的任何人跟我一起去抵制它。

sentences.en: I think they were scared.
sentences.zh: 我想他们是害怕了。

sentences.en: They figured they would lose.
sentences.zh: 他们觉得会输。

sentences.en: A few decades after Lincoln Heights was incorporated, the town fell on hard times.
sentences.zh: 林肯高地建制几十年后，小镇陷入了困境。

sentences.en: First, manufacturing jobs started disappearing in the 1970s.
sentences.zh: 首先，制造业工作在70年代开始消失。

sentences.en: You have the crack epidemic in the 80s, the crime bill in the 90s, and late 90s, early 2000s.
sentences.zh: 80年代有快克毒品泛滥，90年代有犯罪法案，还有90年代末和21世纪初。

sentences.en: It was crazy out here.
sentences.zh: 那时候这里简直疯了。

sentences.en: When Durrance was a kid, the community lost a lot of young people to drugs, gun violence, and prison.
sentences.zh: 杜兰斯小时候，社区里很多年轻人因为毒品、枪支暴力和入狱而丧生。

sentences.en: At the same time as home values rose in the surrounding towns, inside Lincoln Heights, they tanked.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，周边城镇的房价在上涨，而林肯高地内部的房价却暴跌。

sentences.en: It was no longer the place black Cincinnatians wanted to be.
sentences.zh: 这里不再是辛辛那提黑人想住的地方了。

sentences.en: In the year 2000, Cincinnati Magazine ran a feature called The Best Places to Live, ranking all the communities in the metro area.
sentences.zh: 2000年，《辛辛那提杂志》刊登了一篇名为《最佳居住地》的专题报道，对大都会区的所有社区进行了排名。

sentences.en: Lincoln Heights came in at number 84, dead laSt.
sentences.zh: 林肯高地排在第84位，垫底。

sentences.en: Today, its population is less than half the size as it was in 1960, which means there are a lot of abandoned lots and buildings around town.
sentences.zh: 今天，它的人口不到1960年时的一半，这意味着镇上有许多废弃的地块和建筑。

sentences.en: And as life got harder in Lincoln Heights over the decades, the noise from the gun range was also getting worse.
sentences.zh: 随着几十年来林肯高地的生活变得愈发艰难，射击场传来的噪音也越来越严重。

sentences.en: Cincinnati's police force grew by the hundreds in the 60s and 70s.
sentences.zh: 辛辛那提的警察队伍在60和70年代增加了数百人。

sentences.en: And starting in the 90s, the department ramped up its use of military-grade tactical weapons, just like other police forces around the country.
sentences.zh: 从90年代开始，该部门像全国各地的其他警察部队一样，加大了对军用级战术武器的使用。

sentences.en: That meant more and more officers spending more hours training with bigger and bigger weapons, like shotguns, semi-automatic rifles, and sometimes even concussion grenades.
sentences.zh: 这意味着越来越多的警察花更多时间训练，使用越来越大的武器，比如霰弹枪、半自动步枪，有时甚至还有震爆弹。

sentences.en: Today, Cincinnati police spend a cumulative 50,000 hours a year training at the range.
sentences.zh: 如今，辛辛那提警察每年在射击场累计训练5万小时。

sentences.en: And because Lincoln Heights is so small, it's had little choice but to build closer and closer to the edge of the range.
sentences.zh: 而且因为林肯高地太小了，它别无选择，只能越建越靠近射击场的边缘。

sentences.en: There are a lot of reasons why Lincoln Heights has struggled over the years.
sentences.zh: 林肯高地多年来举步维艰的原因有很多。

sentences.en: The nerve-rattling chaos of constant gunfire is one of them.
sentences.zh: 持续不断的枪声带来的神经衰弱般的混乱就是其中之一。

sentences.en: The way land use occurs within these metropolitan areas and regions, Black space is devalued.
sentences.zh: 在这些大都市区和区域内，土地利用的方式导致黑人空间被贬值。

sentences.en: Here's historian Henry Louis Taylor again.
sentences.zh: 历史学家亨利·路易斯·泰勒再次登场。

sentences.en: And the moment you put a gun range next to a community, you have truly devalued that space because you've created structural noise pollution.
sentences.zh: 当你把一个射击场放在一个社区旁边时，你就真正贬低了那个空间，因为你制造了结构性的噪音污染。

sentences.en: My name is Ruby Kinsey Mumfrey.
sentences.zh: 我叫鲁比·金西·芒弗里。

sentences.en: I'm the mayor for the village of Lincoln Heights.
sentences.zh: 我是林肯高地村的村长。

sentences.en: Lifelong resident.
sentences.zh: 我一生都住在这里。

sentences.en: I grew up in Lincoln Heights, born and raised.
sentences.zh: 我在林肯高地长大，土生土长。

sentences.en: Ruby told me that, several years ago, a developer had a plan to build a series of single-family homes in Lincoln Heights.
sentences.zh: 鲁比告诉我，几年前，一位开发商计划在林肯高地建造一系列单户住宅。

sentences.en: The properties would have been a big boost to the town's tax base.
sentences.zh: 这些房产本可以极大地增加该镇的税基。

sentences.en: But once the developer realized how loud the gunfire was, the deal fell through.
sentences.zh: 但当开发商意识到枪声有多大时，这笔交易就告吹了。

sentences.en: Even though Ruby loves this town, there's an alternate history she sometimes imagines.
sentences.zh: 尽管鲁比热爱这个小镇，但她有时会想象另一种历史。

sentences.en: When I go to other communities and stuff, I think about what would Lincoln Heights look like if we didn't have that shooting range?
sentences.zh: 当我去其他社区时，我会想，如果我们没有那个射击场，林肯高地会是什么样子？

sentences.en: And if we would have had that land, what would we be like?
sentences.zh: 如果我们拥有那块土地，我们会是什么样？

sentences.en: What would our population be?
sentences.zh: 我们的人口会是多少？

sentences.en: The closest the town ever came to realizing this vision was back in 1999.
sentences.zh: 该镇最接近实现这一愿景是在1999年。

sentences.en: The mayor of Cincinnati offered to close the range, which sits in a wealthier majority-white suburb called Evendale, right next door to Lincoln Heights.
sentences.zh: 辛辛那提市长提议关闭这个射击场，它位于林肯高地隔壁一个更富裕、以白人为主的郊区——埃文代尔。

sentences.en: Cincinnati would then give some of that land to Lincoln Heights so the town could zone it for commercial use and generate extra tax revenue.
sentences.zh: 辛辛那提随后会将部分土地交给林肯高地，以便该镇将其划为商业用地，产生额外的税收。

sentences.en: But the Cincinnati Police Department was not okay with that.
sentences.zh: 但辛辛那提警察局不同意。

sentences.en: It had no interest in moving the range.
sentences.zh: 它对搬迁射击场毫无兴趣。

sentences.en: The firearms training commander said the facility was too valuable to give away.
sentences.zh: 枪械训练指挥官称，该设施价值太高，不能放弃。

sentences.en: And besides, he said, the noise couldn't really be that bad in Lincoln Heights.
sentences.zh: 而且他还说，林肯高地的噪音不可能真的那么严重。

sentences.en: The president of the police union went even further.
sentences.zh: 警察工会主席甚至更进一步。

sentences.en: He said anyone who supported the plan was spitting on the graves of officers who'd been killed in the line of duty.
sentences.zh: 他说，任何支持该计划的人都是在向殉职警察的坟墓上吐口水。

sentences.en: The talking point has always been, this is a police safety matter, that if you try to take this away, you are against police safety, you're against the police.
sentences.zh: 他们的论调一直是：这是一个警察安全问题，如果你试图拿走它，你就是反对警察安全，反对警察。

sentences.en: It wasn't a real argument.
sentences.zh: 这根本不是真正的论点。

sentences.en: It was emotional gaslighting to keep a gun range, to keep an environmental injustice right outside of a black neighborhood.
sentences.zh: 这是一种情感上的煤气灯操纵，目的是保留一个射击场，在一个黑人社区外维持一种环境不公。

sentences.en: I mean, that's all it was.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，仅此而已。

sentences.en: After all that police pushback, the plan fizzled out.
sentences.zh: 在警察的强烈抵制下，该计划不了了之。

sentences.en: That was almost 25 years ago.
sentences.zh: 那已经是近25年前的事了。

sentences.en: Today, the residents of Lincoln Heights have been hearing that gunfire for nearly eight decades.
sentences.zh: 今天，林肯高地的居民已经听了近八十年的枪声了。

sentences.en: There are people who have lived their whole lives in this town and never known quiet.
sentences.zh: 有些人一辈子都住在这个镇上，从未享受过安静。

sentences.en: Lincoln Heights predicament is extremely rare.
sentences.zh: 林肯高地的困境极为罕见。

sentences.en: Usually, city lawmakers aren't eager to place open-air government-owned shooting ranges in the middle of dense neighborhoods
sentences.zh: 通常，城市立法者并不急于在人口稠密的社区中间设置露天的政府所属射击场，

sentences.en: because the people who live there would get fed up and vote them out.
sentences.zh: 因为住在那里的人会受够了并把他们选下去。

sentences.en: That is the heart of the problem in Lincoln Heights.
sentences.zh: 这就是林肯高地问题的核心。

sentences.en: Cincinnati owns the range, and Lincoln Heights residents don't vote in Cincinnati.
sentences.zh: 辛辛那提拥有这个射击场，而林肯高地的居民在辛辛那提没有投票权。

sentences.en: And the land that the range sits on isn't in Lincoln Heights or Cincinnati.
sentences.zh: 而且射击场所在的土地既不在林肯高地，也不在辛辛那提。

sentences.en: It's in a third town.
sentences.zh: 它在第三个镇。

sentences.en: But hardly anyone who lives in that town can hear the gunfire because their residential areas are way off in another part of the community.
sentences.zh: 但住在那个镇上的人几乎没人能听到枪声，因为他们的住宅区在社区的另一端。

sentences.en: So, no one with the power to move the gun range is directly accountable to the people who have to live with the noise.
sentences.zh: 所以，任何有权搬迁射击场的人，都不直接对那些必须忍受噪音的人负责。

sentences.en: The people of Lincoln Heights.
sentences.zh: 也就是林肯高地的人民。

sentences.en: This type of cross-jurisdictional conflict happens all the time, whether it's between neighbors who share a fence or nations that share a border.
sentences.zh: 这种跨司法管辖区的冲突时有发生，无论是共享围栏的邻居之间，还是共享边界的国家之间。

sentences.en: Pollution, noise, a hideous display of lawn ornaments.
sentences.zh: 污染、噪音、丑陋的草坪装饰展示。

sentences.en: If someone is producing it on their own land, they don't always have to listen to you when you ask them to stop.
sentences.zh: 如果有人在自己的土地上制造这些，当你要求他们停止时，他们并不总是会听你的。

sentences.en: So, we're in Mariana Terrace, so we're literally like another fence line apart from us in the shooting range right now.
sentences.zh: 我们现在在玛丽安娜露台，所以我们离射击场真的只隔了一道围栏。

sentences.en: When I visited Lincoln Heights, Durrance took me to one of the corners of town that gets the worst of the gunfire.
sentences.zh: 当我访问林肯高地时，杜兰斯带我去了镇上受枪声影响最严重的角落之一。

sentences.en: It's called Mariana Terrace.
sentences.zh: 它叫玛丽安娜露台。

sentences.en: It's a public housing complex with 76 units spread across a few low-lying apartment buildings and townhouses.
sentences.zh: 这是一个公共住房综合体，有76个单元，分布在几栋低矮的公寓楼和联排别墅中。

sentences.en: On one side of the development is a playground and I-75, which goes down to Cincinnati.
sentences.zh: 开发区的一侧是一个游乐场和通往辛辛那提的75号州际公路。

sentences.en: On another side is a long chain-link fence, the edge of the gun range.
sentences.zh: 另一侧是一道长长的铁丝网围栏，那是射击场的边缘。

sentences.en: So, it might be just a little separation from about 50 feet between us and the shooting.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们和射击场之间可能只有大约50英尺的距离。

sentences.en: But once again, the direction that we're...
sentences.zh: 但再一次，我们所处的方向……

sentences.en: At one end of the gun range, there's a wall that's supposed to dampen the noise so it won't bother one of the other towns nearby.
sentences.zh: 在射击场的一端，有一堵墙，本意是用来减弱噪音，以免打扰附近的其他城镇。

sentences.en: But for Mariana Terrace, that wall has had the exact opposite effect.
sentences.zh: 但对于玛丽安娜露台来说，那堵墙产生了完全相反的效果。

sentences.en: The sound is amplified because where their wall is, it projects and echoes those sounds back.
sentences.zh: 声音被放大了，因为墙的位置会将那些声音反射并回荡回来。

sentences.en: So, we don't just get the initial boom, we get that and the echo pushing back towards Lincoln Heights.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们不仅听到了最初的爆炸声，还听到了回声向林肯高地推回。

sentences.en: You can probably hear the gunfire in the background of that clip.
sentences.zh: 你可能在那个片段的背景里听到了枪声。

sentences.en: But I assure you, in person, it's way louder and a little scary if you're not used to it.
sentences.zh: 但我向你保证，亲临现场的话，声音要大得多，如果你不习惯，还会有点吓人。

sentences.en: There's been quite a bit of research on the effects of sustained loud noise on the nervous system.
sentences.zh: 关于持续高分贝噪音对神经系统的影响，已经有不少研究了。

sentences.en: As you might imagine, none of those effects are good.
sentences.zh: 正如你所料，这些影响没有一个是好的。

sentences.en: Background noise can impair a kid's cognitive performance.
sentences.zh: 背景噪音会损害孩子的认知表现。

sentences.en: It can cause chronic stress and hypertension.
sentences.zh: 它会导致慢性压力和高血压。

sentences.en: And, of course, it's not great for your ears.
sentences.zh: 当然，这对你的耳朵也不好。

sentences.en: Regular exposure to sounds louder than 85 decibels can cause hearing loss over time.
sentences.zh: 长期暴露在超过85分贝的声音中会导致听力受损。

sentences.en: An audiologist from the University of Cincinnati went to Lincoln Heights and made a recording of gunfire noise in the neighborhood.
sentences.zh: 辛辛那提大学的一位听力学家来到林肯高地，录下了社区里的枪声。

sentences.en: It repeatedly spiked to over 100 decibels, louder than a construction site.
sentences.zh: 它反复飙升到100分贝以上，比建筑工地还要吵。

sentences.en: I can't actually, as an entrepreneur, it's very hard to work from home and try to get anything done.
sentences.zh: 作为一个创业者，我真的很难在家工作并完成任何事情。

sentences.en: Like, I do multiple different things and this is constantly, you know, all day, every day.
sentences.zh: 我同时做很多不同的事情，而这声音是持续不断的，你知道，每天整天都是这样。

sentences.en: Alonda Brooks has lived in the complex for eight years with her three kids.
sentences.zh: 阿隆达·布鲁克斯带着三个孩子在这个小区住了八年。

sentences.en: Actually, a lot of people on this side of the street work nights.
sentences.zh: 其实，这条街这边很多人都是上夜班的。

sentences.en: How do you get any rest during the day?
sentences.zh: 你白天怎么休息呢？

sentences.en: It's no way to muffle it even inside of your home.
sentences.zh: 即使在家里也根本无法隔音。

sentences.en: So, it's really bad, like, to the point where you can be having a conversation with somebody inside of your home with the doors closed and everything.
sentences.zh: 所以真的很糟糕，严重到你在家里关着门和别人说话时，

sentences.en: And they're like, oh, my God, what is that?
sentences.zh: 他们会说，天哪，那是什么声音？

sentences.en: You tell people all the time, like, I live at the back of a gun range and they're like, wow, that's crazy.
sentences.zh: 你总是告诉别人，我住在射击场后面，他们会说，哇，那太疯狂了。

sentences.en: It's traumatizing.
sentences.zh: 这是一种创伤。

sentences.en: Do you ever feel like you don't want to bring people to your house because of that?
sentences.zh: 你是否曾因为这个而不愿带人来家里？

sentences.en: Oh, yeah, no, I don't really have any people.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的，不，我真的没什么人来往。

sentences.en: I don't have visitors.
sentences.zh: 我没有访客。

sentences.en: When we drove away from the complex, Durant's told me he's not a gun guy, but he's learned a lot about firearms from listening to the range his whole life.
sentences.zh: 当我们开车离开小区时，杜兰斯告诉我他不是个枪迷，但他一生都在听射击场的声音，所以对枪械了解很多。

sentences.en: He talks about it like it's the weather.
sentences.zh: 他谈论它就像谈论天气一样。

sentences.en: There are good days and bad days and none of it is under your control.
sentences.zh: 有好日子也有坏日子，而且这一切都不受你控制。

sentences.en: Yeah, so today's a light day.
sentences.zh: 是的，所以今天是个轻松的日子。

sentences.en: So, you probably maybe have about maybe three or four officers using their hand weapons, just their nine millimeters, but you can still hear the intensity of the sound.
sentences.zh: 所以可能只有三四个警察在使用手枪，就是他们的9毫米手枪，但你仍然能听到声音的强度。

sentences.en: It's just a pop out, pop out, pop out, pop out.
sentences.zh: 就是砰、砰、砰、砰的声音。

sentences.en: There's days where they're using, like, the shotgun weapon days are bad.
sentences.zh: 有些日子他们会用霰弹枪，那些日子很糟糕。

sentences.en: Your automatic rifle days are bad.
sentences.zh: 自动步枪的日子也很糟糕。

sentences.en: Like, those are just the constant, you know.
sentences.zh: 就像，那些都是持续不断的，你知道的。

sentences.en: A lot of people in Lincoln Heights have their own horror stories about the gun range.
sentences.zh: 林肯高地的许多人都有关于射击场的恐怖故事。

sentences.en: Some people remember times when there were real shootings in the community and the victims were hurt.
sentences.zh: 有些人记得社区里发生过真正的枪击事件，受害者受伤的时候。

sentences.en: But because everyone who heard the shots just assumed they came from the range, the emergency response was delayed.
sentences.zh: 但因为每个听到枪声的人都以为是射击场传来的，所以紧急响应被延误了。

sentences.en: And then there was the time in 2008 when a stray bullet escaped from the range and broke the windshield of a car parked nearby.
sentences.zh: 还有2008年那次，一颗流弹从射击场飞出，打碎了附近一辆汽车的挡风玻璃。

sentences.en: Parents in Lincoln Heights worry about possible lead in the soil and water from all those bullets in the ground.
sentences.zh: 林肯高地的父母担心地里所有的子弹会导致土壤和水中含有铅。

sentences.en: And kids in town have a history of busting through the chain-link fence and sneaking onto the range to collect bullet casings as a game.
sentences.zh: 镇上的孩子们过去常常冲破铁丝网，溜进射击场收集弹壳当作游戏。

sentences.en: And the gunfire you hear in Lincoln Heights is not just any gunfire.
sentences.zh: 而且你在林肯高地听到的枪声不仅仅是普通的枪声。

sentences.en: It's police gunfire, which makes the range feel even more intimidating.
sentences.zh: 那是警察的枪声，这让射击场感觉更加令人生畏。

sentences.en: I don't even know how to put it into words.
sentences.zh: 我甚至不知道该怎么用语言来表达。

sentences.en: It's kind of like a traumatizing experience, even through adulthood.
sentences.zh: 这就像是一种创伤性的经历，即使到了成年也是如此。

sentences.en: Alicia Franklin grew up in Lincoln Heights, and now she's raising her kids there, four black boys.
sentences.zh: 艾丽西亚·富兰克林在林肯高地长大，现在她正在那里抚养她的四个黑人男孩。

sentences.en: Conversations with my sons have kind of looked something like,
sentences.zh: 我和儿子们的对话大概是这样的：

sentences.en: Okay, we have the gun range.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我们有这个射击场。

sentences.en: That's the gunfire you're hearing.
sentences.zh: 那就是你听到的枪声。

sentences.en: The reason that the police have the gun range is so that they can practice.
sentences.zh: 警察有这个射击场是为了练习。

sentences.en: Now, when you possibly get into some kind of trouble, there could possibly be an escalated situation.
sentences.zh: 现在，当你可能遇到某种麻烦时，可能会出现升级的情况。

sentences.en: And police shoot black men for no reason.
sentences.zh: 而警察会无缘无故地射杀黑人。

sentences.en: Followed up with, well, why?
sentences.zh: 接着是，嗯，为什么？

sentences.en: Which is typical for a kid.
sentences.zh: 这对孩子来说很典型。

sentences.en: And there's no way that you can explain it.
sentences.zh: 你根本无法解释。

sentences.en: And so it's basically like you're saying, they're using this range as target practice for you.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上就像你在说，他们把这个射击场当作针对你们的靶场练习。

sentences.en: Like a lot of communities in the U.S., the Cincinnati area has seen multiple black men killed by police officers over the years.
sentences.zh: 像美国许多社区一样，辛辛那提地区多年来目睹了多名黑人被警察杀害。

sentences.en: I also have a five-year-old.
sentences.zh: 我还有一个五岁的孩子。

sentences.en: Now the five-year-old is questioning.
sentences.zh: 现在五岁的孩子也在质疑。

sentences.en: Like, Mom, what's that noise?
sentences.zh: 就像，妈妈，那是什么声音？

sentences.en: He hears guns, and he knows that they are associated with violence.
sentences.zh: 他听到了枪声，也知道这些枪声与暴力有关。

sentences.en: And it makes me feel helpless because there's not really anything that I can do except move.
sentences.zh: 这让我感到无助，因为除了搬走，我真的什么也做不了。

sentences.en: People like Alicia had grown up hearing the legend of Lincoln Heights,
sentences.zh: 像艾丽西亚这样的人，从小就是听着林肯高地的传奇长大的，

sentences.en: how it was built from scratch by black migrants who'd escaped Jim Crow and sacrificed everything just to have some real control over their own community.
sentences.zh: 听着它是如何由逃离吉姆·克劳法案的黑人移民白手起家建立起来的，他们牺牲了一切，只为了能真正掌控自己的社区。

sentences.en: But the gun range has made many of the residents feel powerless.
sentences.zh: 但射击场让许多居民感到无能为力。

sentences.en: Historian Henry Louis Taylor says that's not just a feeling.
sentences.zh: 历史学家亨利·路易斯·泰勒说，这不仅仅是一种感觉。

sentences.en: To some extent, it's reality.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，这是现实。

sentences.en: The idea of controlling the space that you live is a very, very powerful idea among any African-American population.
sentences.zh: 掌控自己居住的空间，这对任何非裔美国人群体来说都是一个非常、非常有力的想法。

sentences.en: But there's a limit to what you can do with that level of control when everything else is outside of your power.
sentences.zh: 但当其他一切都超出你的掌控范围时，这种掌控力能做的事情是有限的。

sentences.en: And that's what we learn from the experience of Lincoln Heights.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们从林肯高地的经历中所学到的。

sentences.en: Over the course of eight decades, people have tried again and again to move the gun range.
sentences.zh: 在过去的八十年里，人们一次又一次地试图搬走这个射击场。

sentences.en: Durrance's grandfather led that fight back in the 1970s.
sentences.zh: 杜兰斯的祖父在 20 世纪 70 年代就领导过那场斗争。

sentences.en: The mayor of Cincinnati tried in the 90s.
sentences.zh: 辛辛那提市长在 90 年代也尝试过。

sentences.en: Every effort failed.
sentences.zh: 所有的努力都失败了。

sentences.en: And then in 2019, a new movement took off in Lincoln Heights.
sentences.zh: 然后在 2019 年，一场新的运动在林肯高地兴起了。

sentences.en: And the energy behind that effort was unlike anything the town had ever seen before.
sentences.zh: 而推动这场运动的能量是这个城镇以前从未见过的。

sentences.en: That is coming up after the break.
sentences.zh: 休息之后，我们将继续讲述。

sentences.en: Lincoln Heights Councilman Durrance Daniels and Mayor Ruby Kenzie Mumfrey had both lived with the gun range for their whole lives.
sentences.zh: 林肯高地议员杜兰斯·丹尼尔斯和市长鲁比·肯齐·芒弗里一生都生活在射击场的阴影下。

sentences.en: By 2019, they were starting to see it as more than a source of traumatizing noise pollution.
sentences.zh: 到了 2019 年，他们开始意识到这不仅仅是令人创伤的噪音污染源。

sentences.en: The firing range, they believed, was an existential threat to the town's survival.
sentences.zh: 他们认为，这个射击场对该镇的生存构成了生存威胁。

sentences.en: The population had been shrinking since the 1970s because who wants to stay in a place,
sentences.zh: 自 20 世纪 70 年代以来，人口一直在减少，因为谁愿意待在一个地方，

sentences.en: much less moved to a place, that constantly sounds like it's under siege.
sentences.zh: 更不用说搬到一个听起来像是时刻处于被围困状态的地方了。

sentences.en: If Lincoln Heights fails, it's our fault.
sentences.zh: 如果林肯高地失败了，那是我们的错。

sentences.en: It's not our grandparents' fault anymore.
sentences.zh: 不再是我们祖父母的错。

sentences.en: Not our parents' fault anymore.
sentences.zh: 不再是我们父母的错。

sentences.en: Can't blame the kids.
sentences.zh: 不能怪孩子们。

sentences.en: It's on us now.
sentences.zh: 现在责任在我们身上。

sentences.en: With that mindset, Durrance put his head down and got to work.
sentences.zh: 抱着这种心态，杜兰斯埋头苦干。

sentences.en: In March 2019, on his 32nd birthday, he showed up at an open meeting of the Cincinnati City Council.
sentences.zh: 2019 年 3 月，在他 32 岁生日那天，他出现在辛辛那提市议会的公开会议上。

sentences.en: And that the constant hearing of bang, bang, bang throughout the whole community echoing is a problem.
sentences.zh: 整个社区不断回荡着砰、砰、砰的枪声，这是一个问题。

sentences.en: I have young kids that can tell you the sound of an automatic rifle, which kind of gun that is, before they can do their ABCs.
sentences.zh: 我的孩子在学会认字母表之前，就能分辨出自动步枪的声音，知道那是哪种枪。

sentences.en: I have kids that have a playground.
sentences.zh: 我有孩子，他们有游乐场。

sentences.en: Durrance was asking the Cincinnati council members to show some empathy.
sentences.zh: 杜兰斯要求辛辛那提的议员们表现出一些同理心。

sentences.en: Just kind of pleading them, like, hey, from one council member to another, do you guys know that you're even down here shooting?
sentences.zh: 就像是在恳求他们，嘿，作为议员，你们知道你们在这里射击吗？

sentences.en: A lot of the councilmen didn't even know where they practiced that.
sentences.zh: 很多议员甚至不知道他们在哪里练习射击。

sentences.en: It was like, wait, we have a gun range in Lincoln Heights?
sentences.zh: 当时的感觉是，等等，我们在林肯高地有一个射击场？

sentences.en: To Durrance, this was the crux of the problem.
sentences.zh: 对杜兰斯来说，这就是问题的症结所在。

sentences.en: The gun range wasn't affecting any residents of Cincinnati, so no one was complaining about it to Cincinnati lawmakers.
sentences.zh: 射击场没有影响到辛辛那提的任何居民，所以没有人向辛辛那提的立法者投诉。

sentences.en: So they had no reason to think about it.
sentences.zh: 所以他们没有理由去考虑这个问题。

sentences.en: Later that year, Ruby, the mayor of Lincoln Heights, teamed up with the mayors of the other towns around the gun range
sentences.zh: 那年晚些时候，林肯高地市长鲁比与射击场周围其他城镇的市长联手，

sentences.en: to send a letter to the Cincinnati mayor asking for relief.
sentences.zh: 致信辛辛那提市长寻求帮助。

sentences.en: They went down to City Hall to make their case to the council, too.
sentences.zh: 他们也去了市政厅向议会陈述他们的理由。

sentences.en: But Cincinnati was not ready to budge.
sentences.zh: 但辛辛那提方面并不打算让步。

sentences.en: The vice mayor of the city said, if the residents of Lincoln Heights wanted the gun range to move,
sentences.zh: 该市副市长表示，如果林肯高地的居民想搬走射击场，

sentences.en: they should be prepared to pay for it themselves.
sentences.zh: 他们应该准备好自己掏钱。

sentences.en: The facility had been there since the 1940s.
sentences.zh: 该设施自 20 世纪 40 年代以来就一直存在。

sentences.en: It was Lincoln Heights that made the decision to keep building next to the range, the vice mayor said.
sentences.zh: 副市长说，是林肯高地决定在射击场旁边继续建设的。

sentences.en: Basically, it's your fault, not ours.
sentences.zh: 基本上，这是你们的错，不是我们的。

sentences.en: That argument doesn't hold water.
sentences.zh: 这种说法站不住脚。

sentences.en: The founders of Lincoln Heights were living in that area long before Cincinnati police started shooting there.
sentences.zh: 林肯高地的创始人在辛辛那提警察开始在那里射击之前很久就住在那一带了。

sentences.en: And because they only got a tiny fraction of the land they wanted to incorporate,
sentences.zh: 而且因为他们只获得了他们想要合并的土地的一小部分，

sentences.en: they had no choice but to build right up to the border of the gun range.
sentences.zh: 他们别无选择，只能紧挨着射击场的边界建造房屋。

sentences.en: So Durrance had truth on his side.
sentences.zh: 所以杜兰斯站在真理这一边。

sentences.en: But he knew that, compared to Cincinnati, Lincoln Heights was small.
sentences.zh: 但他知道，与辛辛那提相比，林肯高地很小。

sentences.en: If it wanted to make itself heard, it needed allies in its corner.
sentences.zh: 如果想让自己的声音被听到，就需要盟友的支持。

sentences.en: So when U.S.
sentences.zh: 所以当美国参议员谢罗德·布朗来到该地区谈论医疗保健时，

sentences.en: Senator Sherrod Brown came to the area to talk about health care, Durrance showed up and raised his hand.
sentences.zh: 杜兰斯出现了并举手提问。

sentences.en: I've never been bashful to ask a question, especially if you're an elected official.
sentences.zh: 我从来不羞于提问，尤其是面对民选官员时。

sentences.en: You know, I wouldn't be doing my job if I didn't ask the question.
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果我不问这个问题，我就没有尽到我的职责。

sentences.en: Durrance asked the senator, speaking of health care,
sentences.zh: 杜兰斯问参议员，说到医疗保健，

sentences.en: did you know there's an open-air, government-owned gun range in your own state that's causing health problems in my town?
sentences.zh: 你知道在你们州有一个政府所有的露天射击场，正在给我的城镇带来健康问题吗？

sentences.en: Senator Brown was shocked.
sentences.zh: 布朗参议员感到震惊。

sentences.en: His staff said there might be federal money available to relocate the gun range,
sentences.zh: 他的工作人员说，可能有联邦资金可以用来搬迁射击场，

sentences.en: especially because federal officers practiced there, too.
sentences.zh: 特别是因为联邦官员也在那里练习。

sentences.en: He was very aggressive on, let's do something about it.
sentences.zh: 他非常积极地表示，让我们为此做点什么吧。

sentences.en: By this point, Durrance and Ruby had been pressing their case for the better part of a year.
sentences.zh: 到这个时候，杜兰斯和鲁比已经为他们的诉求奔走了大半年了。

sentences.en: They'd spent all this time making appearances at City Hall,
sentences.zh: 他们花了很多时间在市政厅露面，

sentences.en: educating Cincinnati council members,
sentences.zh: 教育辛辛那提的议员们，

sentences.en: and recruiting supporters from other towns in the county.
sentences.zh: 并招募了县里其他城镇的支持者。

sentences.en: And now, they had the backing of a U.S.
sentences.zh: 现在，他们有了美国参议员的支持。

sentences.en: senator.
sentences.zh: 这场运动似乎终于有了势头。

sentences.en: The movement seemed like it was finally gaining momentum.
sentences.zh: 然后，在 2020 年 3 月，新冠疫情爆发了。

sentences.en: Then, in March 2020, COVID hit.
sentences.zh: 突然之间，孩子们在餐桌上上学。

sentences.en: All of a sudden, kids were going to school at their kitchen tables.
sentences.zh: 人们如果可以的话都在家工作。

sentences.en: People were working from home if they could.
sentences.zh: 在林肯高地，这意味着无法逃避枪声。

sentences.en: In Lincoln Heights, that meant no escape from the gunfire.
sentences.zh: 即使你以前习惯了，现在也真的注意到了。

sentences.en: Even if you were used to it before, you really noticed it now.
sentences.zh: 对于像艾丽西亚·富兰克林这样的终身居民来说，紧迫感正在增强。

sentences.en: For lifelong residents like Alicia Franklin, a sense of urgency was building.
sentences.zh: 因为现在你整天都能听到它。

sentences.en: Because now you're hearing it all day.
sentences.zh: 你没法离开家，然后，你知道，获得一点安宁。

sentences.en: You don't get to leave home and then, you know, have a little bit of peace.
sentences.zh: 不，你整天甚至深夜都能听到它。

sentences.en: No, you're hearing it all day into the night.
sentences.zh: 很快，每当林肯高地的居民打开电视，

sentences.zh: 就会有一条新闻和一段可怕的视频占据了广播频道。

sentences.en: there was one news story and one horrifying video dominating the airwaves.
sentences.zh: 周六，乔治·弗洛伊德之死引发的抗议浪潮从海岸蔓延到海岸，

sentences.zh: 纪念我们居民的最好方式，

sentences.en: was to be more aggressive with the situation.

sentences.en: The four-year-old, who you all saw on the video,
sentences.zh: 他以前听到枪声时会受到惊吓。

sentences.en: he used to get startled and scared when he heard those gunshots.
sentences.zh: 那段视频拍摄的时间并不久远。

sentences.en: And that video wasn't long ago.
sentences.zh: 现在，这些声音对他来说已经习以为常了，这非常令人担忧。

sentences.en: Now, they don't faze him, which is very concerning.
sentences.zh: 听力学专家布莱恩·厄尔也在听证会上发言。

sentences.en: Audiology expert Brian Earle also spoke at the hearing.
sentences.zh: 他告诉议会，有一次他访问林肯高地，

sentences.en: He told the council about one time he visited Lincoln Heights
sentences.zh: 测量射击场附近的声级。

sentences.en: to measure the sound levels near the range.
sentences.zh: 我的眼睛睁大了，耳朵开始颤动。

sentences.en: My eyes widened, and my ears started to flutter.
sentences.zh: 我们有一种所谓的声反射，

sentences.en: We have what is called an acoustic reflex
sentences.zh: 当我们的身体告诉我们声音太大了时，它就会开始触发。

sentences.en: that starts to trigger when our bodies are telling us that it's too much.
sentences.zh: 我的耳朵在远处就有这种反应，

sentences.en: My ears were doing that from a distance,
sentences.zh: 但在我和射击场之间，是一个住宅区和一个游乐场。

sentences.en: but in between me and the range was a housing development and a playground.
sentences.zh: 所以作为父亲，我感到这太近了。

sentences.en: So there's the father in me, but it's too close.
sentences.zh: 你可以在那段视频片段中听到布莱恩有些哽咽。

sentences.en: You can hear Brian getting a little choked up in that clip.
sentences.zh: 几年前我采访他时也发生过这种情况。

sentences.en: It happened when I interviewed him a couple years ago, too.
sentences.zh: 看到林肯高地的孩子们对那些让他耳朵抽搐的噪音毫无反应，

sentences.en: Seeing children in Lincoln Heights not even reacting to the noise
sentences.zh: 这让他几乎无法承受。

sentences.en: that was making his ears twitch,
sentences.zh: 他访问的住宅区是玛丽安娜露台，

sentences.en: it was almost too much for him to bear.
sentences.zh: 也就是我和杜兰斯去过的地方。

sentences.en: The housing development he visited was Mariana Terrace,
sentences.zh: 杜兰斯也参加了听证会。

sentences.en: the same place I went with Durantz.
sentences.zh: 他发表了自己的证词。

sentences.en: Durantz was at the hearing, too.
sentences.zh: 我教橄榄球。

sentences.en: He gave his own testimony.
sentences.zh: 我在小学教书。

sentences.en: I coach football.
sentences.zh: 我经历过这一切。

sentences.en: I teach at the elementary school.
sentences.zh: 我父亲经历过这一切。

sentences.en: I've lived through it.
sentences.zh: 我祖父经历过这一切。

sentences.en: My dad lived through it.
sentences.zh: 为什么我的儿子也要经历这一切？

sentences.en: My grandfather lived through it.
sentences.zh: 这根本说不通。

sentences.en: Why does my son have to live through it, too?
sentences.zh: 你听到了那些废话，伙计。

sentences.en: It doesn't make any sense.
sentences.zh: 你听到了那些废话，伙计。

sentences.en: You heard that crap, man.
sentences.zh: 你听到了那些废话，伙计。

sentences.en: Nobody wants to live in that.
sentences.zh: 没人想住在那种地方。

sentences.en: You are killing us.
sentences.zh: 你们这是在折磨我们。

sentences.en: Through stress.
sentences.zh: 在压力之下。

sentences.en: I'm sorry if I look like I'm animated right now,
sentences.zh: 如果我看起来情绪激动，我很抱歉，

sentences.en: but I'm not playing.
sentences.zh: 但我不是在开玩笑。

sentences.en: We ain't playing.
sentences.zh: 我们不是在开玩笑。

sentences.en: The residents of Lincoln Heights had been trying to get
sentences.zh: 林肯高地的居民几乎从这个城镇建立之初，

sentences.en: rid of the gun range for almost as long as the town had existed.
sentences.zh: 就一直试图摆脱那个射击场。

sentences.en: But now, finally, after this hearing,
sentences.zh: 但现在，终于，在这次听证会之后，

sentences.en: the generations-long gridlock seemed to dissipate.
sentences.zh: 那持续了几代人的僵局似乎要化解了。

sentences.en: Even the Cincinnati police,
sentences.zh: 就连辛辛那提警方，

sentences.en: which had long refused to relocate the range,
sentences.zh: 此前一直拒绝搬迁射击场，

sentences.en: now said it was officially open to the idea.
sentences.zh: 现在也表示正式对这个想法持开放态度。

sentences.en: The city of Cincinnati began searching for a new place for its police to train,
sentences.zh: 辛辛那提市开始为警察寻找新的训练场地，

sentences.en: and it landed on a location in a less-densely populated township
sentences.zh: 最终选定了一个人口密度较低的乡镇，

sentences.en: just a few miles west of Lincoln Heights.
sentences.zh: 就在林肯高地以西几英里处。

sentences.en: The advantage of the new location is there is actually already an open-air firing range there
sentences.zh: 这个新地点的优势在于，那里实际上已经有一个露天射击场了，

sentences.en: where the county sheriff's department trains.
sentences.zh: 县治安官部门就在那里训练。

sentences.en: Now there are plans in the works to expand that facility
sentences.zh: 现在已有计划扩建该设施，

sentences.en: so Cincinnati police can train there, too.
sentences.zh: 这样辛辛那提警察也可以在那里训练。

sentences.en: It's such a simple solution.
sentences.zh: 这是一个如此简单的解决方案。

sentences.en: Elegant, almoSt.
sentences.zh: 甚至可以说是优雅。

sentences.en: The cops will get a brand-new facility,
sentences.zh: 警察将获得一个全新的设施，

sentences.en: and Lincoln Heights will get some peace and closure.
sentences.zh: 而林肯高地将获得安宁与了结。

sentences.en: It almost makes you wonder why it took so long for Cincinnati to come around.
sentences.zh: 这不禁让人纳闷，为什么辛辛那提花了这么久才想通。

sentences.en: The move will cost about $31.5 million.
sentences.zh: 这次搬迁将耗资约3150万美元。

sentences.en: Cincinnati only agreed to chip in about $4 million.
sentences.zh: 辛辛那提只同意出资约400万美元。

sentences.en: The rest is coming from the state,
sentences.zh: 其余资金来自州政府、

sentences.en: the federal government, and the county.
sentences.zh: 联邦政府和县政府。

sentences.en: I asked the Cincinnati police for comment,
sentences.zh: 我曾要求辛辛那提警方置评，

sentences.en: but I haven't heard back.
sentences.zh: 但没有收到回复。

sentences.en: This past January, the county officially announced the plans for the new range
sentences.zh: 今年一月，县政府正式宣布了新射击场的计划，

sentences.en: and the expected closure of the old one next to Lincoln Heights.
sentences.zh: 以及预计将关闭林肯高地旁旧射击场的消息。

sentences.en: Alicia Franklin saw Durant's post about it on Facebook.
sentences.zh: 艾丽西亚·富兰克林在Facebook上看到了杜兰特发布的帖子。

sentences.en: I just really couldn't believe it.
sentences.zh: 我真的简直不敢相信。

sentences.en: I'm like, is this for real?
sentences.zh: 我在想，这是真的吗？

sentences.en: Like, I mean, I was just elated.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我当时欣喜若狂。

sentences.en: I lit up.
sentences.zh: 我整个人都亮了。

sentences.en: Like, this is finally, you know, gonna happen.
sentences.zh: 就像是，你知道，这终于要发生了。

sentences.en: But nobody's planning a victory party just yet.
sentences.zh: 但还没人打算举办庆祝派对。

sentences.en: Durant's told me the most excited he's been so far
sentences.zh: 杜兰特告诉我，他迄今为止最兴奋的时刻，

sentences.en: was the day he called me in January
sentences.zh: 就是一月份他打电话给我，

sentences.en: to tell me about the county's announcement that the range was getting moved.
sentences.zh: 告诉我县政府宣布射击场要搬迁的那天。

sentences.en: But after we hung up, later that day...
sentences.zh: 但我们挂断电话后，那天晚些时候……

sentences.en: I came home.
sentences.zh: 我回到家。

sentences.en: You know what I heard?
sentences.zh: 你知道我听到了什么吗？

sentences.en: He's still out here shooting.
sentences.zh: 他们还在外面射击。

sentences.en: So, you know, you don't get to get too excited
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，你不能太兴奋，

sentences.en: because they're going to consistently remind you that they're still here.
sentences.zh: 因为他们会不断提醒你，他们还在这里。

sentences.en: When I talked to people in Lincoln Heights,
sentences.zh: 当我与林肯高地的居民交谈时，

sentences.en: I heard lots of different opinions about the projected closure of the range.
sentences.zh: 我听到了关于射击场预计关闭的许多不同意见。

sentences.en: Some people think it's definitely going to happen.
sentences.zh: 有些人认为这肯定会发生。

sentences.en: Others think those people are just fooling themselves,
sentences.zh: 另一些人认为这些人只是在自欺欺人，

sentences.en: and they'll believe it when they see it.
sentences.zh: 他们要亲眼看到才会相信。

sentences.en: And a lot of residents think moving the gun range isn't enough.
sentences.zh: 而且许多居民认为搬走射击场还不够。

sentences.en: They say Cincinnati owes Lincoln Heights reparations
sentences.zh: 他们说辛辛那提欠林肯高地赔偿，

sentences.en: for 70-plus years of pain and suffering.
sentences.zh: 为了那70多年来的痛苦和折磨。

sentences.en: There's also a cynical read on this story.
sentences.zh: 关于这个故事，还有一种愤世嫉俗的解读。

sentences.en: Some Lincoln Heights residents believe Cincinnati is moving the range
sentences.zh: 一些林肯高地居民认为辛辛那提搬迁射击场，

sentences.en: less because of public pressure and more as a sensible business deal.
sentences.zh: 与其说是出于公众压力，不如说是一笔精明的商业交易。

sentences.en: Evendale, the town where the gun range sits,
sentences.zh: 埃文代尔，那个射击场所在的城镇，

sentences.en: has been itching for years to reclaim that land from Cincinnati.
sentences.zh: 多年来一直渴望从辛辛那提手中收回那片土地。

sentences.en: They want to use it for industrial development.
sentences.zh: 他们想将其用于工业开发。

sentences.en: Evendale is utilizing and leveraging the efforts
sentences.zh: 埃文代尔正在利用和借力，

sentences.en: that the residents are putting forward to make this happen.
sentences.zh: 居民们为实现这一目标所付出的努力。

sentences.en: But with politics, I think you always try to realize,
sentences.zh: 但在政治上，我认为你总是试图弄明白，

sentences.en: how do you benefit from it?
sentences.zh: 你从中能得到什么好处？

sentences.en: That's just the game that we play.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们玩的游戏。

sentences.en: At the end of the day, a win is a win.
sentences.zh: 归根结底，赢了就是赢了。

sentences.en: Durant says he's already seen a change in the mentality
sentences.zh: 杜兰特说，他已经看到了一些居民心态上的转变，

sentences.en: of some of the residents who helped mobilize against the range.
sentences.zh: 那些曾经参与反对射击场的人。

sentences.en: There's a feeling of power and possibility now
sentences.zh: 现在有一种力量感和可能性，

sentences.en: that wasn't there before.
sentences.zh: 这是以前没有的。

sentences.en: Like, I want the residents to really realize what they did here.
sentences.zh: 就像，我希望居民们真正意识到他们在这里做了什么。

sentences.en: Not only what they did here,
sentences.zh: 不仅是他们在这里做了什么，

sentences.en: but what y'all can do moving forward with this community.
sentences.zh: 还有你们大家在未来能为这个社区做些什么。

sentences.en: Because the community was just an idea 75 years ago.
sentences.zh: 因为这个社区在75年前仅仅是一个想法。

sentences.en: Just a bunch of Black folks that come together and say,
sentences.zh: 只是一群黑人聚在一起说，

sentences.en: we want to provide Black people jobs.
sentences.zh: 我们想为黑人提供就业机会。

sentences.en: And that was just an idea.
sentences.zh: 那仅仅是一个想法。

sentences.en: Now we're still standing here.
sentences.zh: 现在我们依然屹立于此。

sentences.en: And that is now going to lead to who knows what 75 years from now.
sentences.zh: 而这现在将引领未来75年，谁知道会发生什么。

sentences.en: And that's the coolest thing about it, for real, in my perspective.
sentences.zh: 从我的角度来看，这才是最酷的事情，真的。

sentences.en: Today, the gun range on the border of Lincoln Heights is still active.
sentences.zh: 今天，林肯高地边缘的射击场仍在运作。

sentences.en: It'll take at least a year or two for the new facility to open,
sentences.zh: 新设施至少需要一两年才能开放，

sentences.en: knock wood.
sentences.zh: 祈求好运。

sentences.en: And the shots will continue until then.
sentences.zh: 在此之前，枪声将继续响起。

sentences.en: But if all goes to plan,
sentences.zh: 但如果一切按计划进行，

sentences.en: the day the Cincinnati police shoot the last bullet at that range
sentences.zh: 辛辛那提警察在那个射击场打出最后一颗子弹的那一天，

sentences.en: will mark the end of a struggle
sentences.zh: 将标志着一场斗争的结束，

sentences.en: that has been passed down through Lincoln Heights families for generations.
sentences.zh: 这场斗争在林肯高地的家庭中代代相传。

sentences.en: The way Mayor Ruby Kinsey Mumphrey sees it,
sentences.zh: 在鲁比·金西·芒弗雷市长看来，

sentences.en: that would put them one step closer
sentences.zh: 这将使他们更进一步，

sentences.en: to realizing the dream the founders had
sentences.zh: 去实现创始人们的梦想，

sentences.en: for a town in control of its own destiny.
sentences.zh: 建立一个能掌控自己命运的城镇。

sentences.en: You know, I lost my father last year,
sentences.zh: 你知道，我去年失去了父亲，

sentences.en: and I knew he wanted that to go.
sentences.zh: 我知道他希望那个射击场消失。

sentences.en: He would be really happy and proud of me
sentences.zh: 如果他知道我帮忙搬走了那个射击场，

sentences.en: that I helped get that gun range moved.
sentences.zh: 他会为我感到非常高兴和自豪。

sentences.en: And so it's going to be like a new story.
sentences.zh: 所以这将是一个新的故事。

sentences.en: It's going to be like opening the door to a new day.
sentences.zh: 就像开启了新的一天的大门。
